Subject: Recap & next steps - FinApps integration (SDK/auth/routing/tool-calling)

Hi Alex / Marcus -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can move toward a technical deep-dive: 

What we heard / priorities:
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference into FinApps flow to power contextual assistant and automated reconciliations.
- Integration surface: server-side calls from FinApps backend -> Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Hosted API depending on SLA needs.
- Key features you care about: SDK setup + auth (OIDC, API keys, KMS), request routing by tenant, structured output / tool-calling for actions (create-ticket, run-query), and embeddings + reranker for search relevance.
- Non-functional: sub-200ms tail latencies for single-turn user lookups, predictable cost for heavy batch inference (overnight), and audit logs for compliance.

Open questions we flagged for the tech deep-dive:
1) Auth model: do you prefer mTLS between services + per-tenant API key rotation, or an OIDC short-lived token model backed by your IdP?
2) Routing: will requests be routed to a single region or should we plan multi-region fallback?
3) Tool catalog: list of external tools FinApps wants Redwood to call (ticketing, DB queries, internal accounting service). Any existing API contracts we can consume?
4) Embeddings / reranker: expected corpus size and update cadence? Will you push documents or do periodic pulls?

Attachments: integration-proposal-v2.pdf (high-level SLA/architecture) - please review.

Suggested next steps:
- Dylan / Dev to propose a reference architecture and sample tool/function-call definitions.
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week (SE + engineering).
- Marcus - if procurement items (NDA, SOW) are ready we can start parallel review.

Are we good to target Wed 30 Jun for the technical call? If so, what time zone is best (you’re PT, correct)?

Thanks,

--

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming priorities: structured tool-calling to our ticketing system and a reranker for our transaction search are most important this quarter. Embeddings corpus will initially be ~10M documents (historical transactions) with nightly incremental updates.

Answers to your questions:
1) Auth: we prefer OIDC short-lived tokens tied to our IdP (Okta). Long-term we may want per-tenant key rotation.
2) Routing: start single-region (us-west) with automatic failover to us-east for DR.
3) Tool catalog: top three tools are -> Ticketing (internal API at https://api.finapps.com/tickets), Accounting-query service (gRPC), and an internal data fetcher for ledger snapshots (pulls CSV). We’ll share API specs via Drive.
4) Embeddings: nightly push from our ETL is easiest.

Procurement: Marcus is looped for NDA/SOW. We’d like a ballpark for committed throughput pricing if we go Dedicated.

Wed 30 Jun PT works for a deep-dive; morning PT is best.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finapps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - FinApps integration (SDK/auth/routing/tool-calling)

Alex / Marissa -

Thanks - below are concrete integration patterns we typically recommend for the three areas you called out. I’ll walk these in the deep-dive and can share runnable examples from our SDK.

1) SDK setup & auth
- Model: backend services use Redwood server SDK (Node/Python). We recommend OIDC short-lived tokens from FinApps IdP, minted for a service account with constrained scopes (inference:generate, tools:call). Tokens exchanged for Redwood session tokens via our token exchange endpoint. For Dedicated customers we support mTLS for the control plane + per-tenant API keys stored in KMS.
- Pattern: request flow -> FinApps backend obtains OIDC token -> POST to /v1/sessions/exchange -> returns short-lived Redwood token.
- Failure modes: token expiry -> respond 401 -> client retries token exchange once then error to user.

2) Routing / multi-tenant isolation
- Use request headers: x-finapps-tenant, x-request-id. Redwood routing policies can pin tenant -> Dedicated pool or fall back to hosted variants. For multi-region we suggest region preference header and built-in failover routing.

3) Structured output & tool/function calling patterns
- Tool definition model (example):
  - id: ticket_create
  - input_schema: {"title": "string", "body": "string", "priority": "enum"}
  - output_schema: {"ticket_id": "string", "status": "string"}
  - call_url: https://api.finapps.com/tickets/create
  - auth: bearer (use internal service token)

- Tool choice guidance: keep 1) high-trust tools (write actions) guarded behind stronger auth and canary rules, 2) read-only tools allowed more freely.
- Parallel tools: spawn parallel tool calls for independent data pulls (e.g., ledger snapshot + accounting-query) and aggregate results into a prompt or call a reranker. Use request-grouping IDs to correlate.
- Error handling patterns:
  * transient svc failures -> retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts) and circuit-breaker if >X% error rate over 1m.
  * semantic errors (400s) -> return structured error to the LLM so it can either ask for clarification or skip the tool call.
  * partial success -> LLM should be designed to accept partial tool outputs and indicate which tool data was missing.

4) Embeddings & reranker
- Ingestion: nightly batch upload via /v1/embeddings/upsert with doc batch sizes of 1k-5k.
- Reranker pattern: two-stage retrieval (approx nearest-neighbor via FAISS/ANN + Redwood reranker call that takes candidate list and query and returns sorted list with confidence scores).
- Freshness: tag embedding vectors with last_updated timestamp; incremental re-upserts for changed docs.

5) Operational concerns
- Tracing: pass x-trace-id through Redwood SDK; logs will include per-call token counts and latency.
- Cost control: set max tokens per request, use prefix caching for common prompts, and configure batching for high-throughput offline jobs.

Example pseudocode (Node):

// exchange OIDC -> redwood session
const session = await redwood.auth.exchange({ oidc_token: oktaToken });

// call model with tool schema and tool list
const resp = await redwood.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-4o',
  tools: [ticketToolDef, accountingToolDef],
  input: userPrompt,
  routing: { tenant: 'finapps-corp', region: 'us-west' }
});

// handle structured output / tool call request from model
if (resp.invocations?.length) {
  for (const inv of resp.invocations) {
    // validate input against inv.tool.input_schema -> call external API -> return result back to model
  }
}

Attachments: redwood-sdk-auth-diagram.pdf and tool-calling-patterns-notes.pdf (architectural notes).

I’ll prep a short runnable example repo for the call; Dev will help map your API contracts to tool definitions.
